summary: The note compares global educational models for architectural heritage conservation, covering university degrees, vocational apprenticeships, indigenous and community-focused programs, and technology training. It cites many programs launched or updated in September 2023 across the US, Europe, UK, India, Canada, Australia, Asia and Latin America. It concludes that the field needs adaptable curricula combining local culture, technology and practical skills.
one_line: A comparative survey of global heritage conservation education, from degree programs and apprenticeships to technology and public engagement, with many September 2023 launches.
key_facts: Columbia University's Master's Program in Historic Preservation began its latest curriculum on September 3, 2023, adding more hands-on and technology-based preservation methods.
The Institute for Art and Restoration in Florence, Italy, began a new module on September 12, 2023, on digital reconstruction of monuments using simulations to predict and prevent degradation.
John Smith Heritage Services in the UK started a masonry restoration apprenticeship on September 15, 2023, using a learn-by-doing approach under experienced conservators.
The Heritage Conservation Skills Program launched in Delhi on September 20, 2023, formalizes India's "Guru-Shishya" (Master-Apprentice) model to pass on centuries-old techniques.
The Canadian Centre for Architecture in Montreal launched a dual classroom-and-internship program on September 5, 2023, partnering with restoration firms.
The University of Sydney introduced a new component on September 18, 2023, encouraging collaboration with Aboriginal communities and recognizing indigenous conservation methods.
China's Tongji University revamped its heritage curriculum on September 22, 2023, integrating sustainable conservation practices.
Japan's updated model (September 2023) emphasizes disaster resilience; the University of Tokyo offers courses on retrofitting historic buildings against seismic activity.
Université Paris-Sorbonne announced a new Department of Digital Heritage on September 26, 2023.
Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh added a course called "Technology and Heritage Management" on September 10, 2023.
The University of Cuenca in Ecuador started the "Heritage Ambassadors Program" on September 14, 2023, educating local citizens about heritage conservation.
Technologies increasingly taught include Building Information Modelling (BIM), Laser Scanning, and 3D Printing.
